title: Criminology 1  For Law Students Only
mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a type of offence committed by juveniles."
Juvenile delinquency is a type of offence committed by juveniles.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an expression of "rebellion" against inequality and against a system that used the legal system - including the law, the police, court and prison as weapon in the class war."
Working class crime is an expression of "rebellion" against inequality and against a system that used the legal system - including the law, the police, court and prison as weapon in the class war.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the radical tradition of the feminist criminology by a British sociologist, Carol Smart."
The feminist perspective is the radical tradition of the feminist criminology by a British sociologist, Carol Smart.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the very essence of justice."
Equality is the very essence of justice.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a term derived from the Anglo- Saxon word 'lagu', meaning to determine."
Law is a term derived from the Anglo- Saxon word 'lagu', meaning to determine.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are the least likely to get caught because they plan their activities very carefully."
Professional criminals are the least likely to get caught because they plan their activities very carefully.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the structural - functionalism paradigm of Robert k."
The functionalism criminology is the structural - functionalism paradigm of Robert k.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a specific type of person."
The criminal is a specific type of person.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are the acts or conducts that violate the criminal law of the society."
The offenders are the acts or conducts that violate the criminal law of the society.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is defined as any act that violates the law."
Crime is defined as any act that violates the law.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the basis of Marxist' approach to crime."
The Marxism criminology is the basis of Marxist' approach to crime.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a non-violent crime usually involving cheating, or dishonesty in commercial matters."
A white-collar crime is a non-violent crime usually involving cheating, or dishonesty in commercial matters.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are the largest and most important subsystem of the criminal justice system."
The police are the largest and most important subsystem of the criminal justice system.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the component of the subconscious mind that is self-serving, egocentric, and concerned with self-gratification."
The id (instinct gratification) is the component of the subconscious mind that is self-serving, egocentric, and concerned with self-gratification.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the branch of criminology which is concerned with the scientific study of victims."
Victiminology is the branch of criminology which is concerned with the scientific study of victims.
fib: ______ are the second component in the triangular relationship of the criminal justice system.
criminal courts
The criminal courts are the second component in the triangular relationship of the criminal justice system.
______ is a psychological reality; people freely enter a social contract with the state to preserve peace and the consensus: a pleasure- pain motivation.
Free-will
Free-will is a psychological reality; people freely enter a social contract with the state to preserve peace and the consensus: a pleasure- pain motivation.
______ are the defined obligatory and expected behaviours of people in a given situation.
Norms
Norms are the defined obligatory and expected behaviours of people in a given situation.
______ refer to the social norms and expectations for acceptable behaviour.
Rules generally
Rules generally refer to the social norms and expectations for acceptable behaviour.
______ is the ideas of the neo- Marxists.
new criminology
The new criminology is the ideas of the neo- Marxists.
______ is a violation of norms of the land,-a deviation from or failure to conform to the norms.
Deviance
Deviance is a violation of norms of the land,-a deviation from or failure to conform to the norms.
______ is defined as that quantity of goods and services, which make a desired usefulness, and satisfaction derived from it.
Utility
Utility is defined as that quantity of goods and services, which make a desired usefulness, and satisfaction derived from it.
______ is the basis of Sigmund Freud' analysis of crime.
Psychoanalysis criminology
Psychoanalysis criminology is the basis of Sigmund Freud' analysis of crime.
______ is defined as the agency set up by government to define and apply the law, to order its enforcement and to settle disputed points on which individual or groups do not agree.
court
A court is defined as the agency set up by government to define and apply the law, to order its enforcement and to settle disputed points on which individual or groups do not agree.
______ is a serious offence punishable by death, a fine, or confinement in a state or federal prison for more than one year.
felony
A felony is a serious offence punishable by death, a fine, or confinement in a state or federal prison for more than one year.
______ are the abstract, general concepts, central beliefs or ideas that provide a standard by which norms are judged.
Values
Values are the abstract, general concepts, central beliefs or ideas that provide a standard by which norms are judged.
______ is defined as a legal process which involves the procedure of processing the person accused of committing crime from arrest to the final disposal of the case.
criminal justice itself
The criminal justice itself is defined as a legal process which involves the procedure of processing the person accused of committing crime from arrest to the final disposal of the case.
______ is responsible for the custody of the final product in the criminal justice system.
prison
The prison is responsible for the custody of the final product in the criminal justice system.
______ is the basis of Erving Goffman' analysis of crime.
Interactionalism criminology
Interactionalism criminology is the basis of Erving Goffman' analysis of crime.
______ is a deliberate destruction of private and public properties.
Vandalism
Vandalism is a deliberate destruction of private and public properties.
